candidates.label: numberOfEmployees
candidates.comment: The number of employees working for an organization or targeted by a business audience. Also called employee count, workforce size, staff number. Examples: "Company A numberOfEmployees 500", "Small Business B numberOfEmployees 15", "Target Audience C numberOfEmployees '100-500'".

candidates.label: employees
candidates.comment: An employment relation between an organization and the people who work for it. Also called "staff", "workforce", "personnel". Examples: "Organization 'Google' employees 'Thousands of people'", "Company 'Acme Corp' employees 'All its staff'", "Restaurant 'The Bistro' employees 'Its kitchen and wait staff'". Distinct from members, which indicates general affiliations rather than employment relationships.

candidates.label: discount
candidates.comment: A price reduction relation between an order and any discount applied to it. Also called: price reduction, markdown, rebate. Examples: "Online Order" discount "10%", "Bulk Purchase" discount "25 USD", "Promotional Order" discount "Free Shipping".

candidates.label: cutoffTime
candidates.comment: A temporal boundary relation between a service period or shipping delivery time and the time after which orders are no longer processed on that day. Also called: order cutoff, daily processing limit, last order time. Examples: "Same-day Delivery" cutoff time "14:00:00-05:00", "Next-day Shipping" cutoff time "17:00:00Z", "Warehouse Processing" cutoff time "23:30:00-05:00".

candidates.label: employee
candidates.comment: An employment relation between an organization and a person who works for it. Also called "works for", "staff member", "on staff". Examples: "Organization 'Google' employee 'Sundar Pichai'", "Company 'Acme Corp' employee 'Jane Doe'", "Restaurant 'The Bistro' employee 'Chef John'". Distinct from member, which indicates a general affiliation rather than an employment relationship.

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

candidates.label: dissolutionDate
candidates.comment: A dissolution date relation between an organization and the date when it was dissolved. Also called "closure date", "ceased operations date", "disbandment date". Examples: "Company 'Acme Corp' dissolutionDate '2023-01-15'", "Non-profit organization dissolutionDate '2022-07-01'", "Partnership dissolutionDate '2024-03-10'".

candidates.label: department
candidates.comment: An organizational structure relation between an organization and one of its departments. Also called: organizational unit, division, branch. Examples: "University" department "Computer Science Department", "Hospital" department "Emergency Room", "Retail Store" department "Pharmacy".

candidates.label: employmentUnit
candidates.comment: An employment unit relation between a job posting and the organization (department, unit, or facility) where the job is performed. Also called "department", "work unit", "reporting unit". Examples: "Job posting 'Software Engineer' employmentUnit 'Engineering Department'", "Job 'Sales Associate' employmentUnit 'Retail Store #123'", "Job 'HR Specialist' employmentUnit 'Human Resources Division'".

candidates.label: hiringOrganization
candidates.comment: A hiring organization relation between a job posting and the organization or person offering the job. Also called employer, recruiting organization, job provider. Examples: "A job posting has a hiring organization 'Acme Corp'.", "The position is offered by a hiring organization.", "This job posting lists the hiring organization."

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: isPartOfBioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A biochemical part-whole relation indicating that one biochemical entity is a component of another larger biochemical entity. Also called component of biochem entity, contained within biochem entity, element of biochem entity. Examples: A protein domain isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a larger protein'. A subunit isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a protein complex'. A specific gene sequence isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a chromosome'.

candidates.label: subEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger event and a smaller event that is a component or part of it. Also called "part of event", "component event", "nested event", "event within event". Examples: "The conference has subEvent a keynote speech", "The festival's subEvent is a specific concert", "This event includes a subEvent workshop.". Distinct from superEvent, which points from the smaller event to the larger one.

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: hasBioChemEntityPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a biochemical entity and one of its constituent biochemical entities. Also called composed of, contains, includes part, made of. Examples: "A protein has a BioChemEntity part of an amino acid sequence.", "A cell has BioChemEntity parts like organelles.", "A molecule has BioChemEntity parts of atoms."

candidates.label: partOfSystem
candidates.comment: A biological relation between an anatomical structure and the anatomical or organ system it is a component of. Also called is a component of, belongs to, is found in, forms part of. Examples: The heart is part of the circulatory system. The lungs are part of the respiratory system. A bone is part of the skeletal system.

candidates.label: subEvents
candidates.comment: A collection of hierarchical relations between a larger event and multiple smaller events that are components or parts of it. Also called "component events", "nested events", "events within event", "parts of event". Examples: "The conference has subEvents multiple presentations", "The festival's subEvents include several concerts and workshops", "This event comprises many subEvents.". Distinct from subEvent, which refers to a single component event.

candidates.label: subStructure
candidates.comment: A component relation between an anatomical structure and the smaller anatomical structures that comprise it. Also called "component structure", "anatomical part", "composed of", "contains structure". Examples: "The heart has subStructure atria", "The brain's subStructure includes the cerebrum", "This anatomical structure is made up of several subStructure elements."

candidates.label: ingredients
candidates.comment: A component relation between a recipe and the individual food items or substances required for its preparation. Also called components, recipe items, constituents, elements. Examples: A cake recipe lists 'flour' as an ingredient. A soup recipe lists 'carrots' as an ingredient. A cocktail recipe lists 'gin' as an ingredient.

candidates.label: superEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a smaller event and the larger event of which it is a part. Also called "part of larger event", "parent event", "contained within event", "main event". Examples: "The concert has superEvent the music festival", "The presentation's superEvent is the conference", "This workshop is part of a superEvent summit.". Distinct from subEvent, which points from the larger event to the smaller one.

candidates.comment: A composition relation between an offer or product collection and the specific products and their quantities it contains. Also called composed of, contains, comprises, consists of, has as object. Examples: An offer includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 2 apples. A product collection includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 5 books. A demand includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 1 car.

candidates.label: containsPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and another smaller place that it contains. Also called "includes place", "encompasses", "holds". Examples: "Country 'France' containsPlace 'Paris'", "City 'Paris' containsPlace 'Eiffel Tower'". Distinct from containedIn or containedInPlace, which are the inverse relations.

candidates.label: mainEntity
candidates.comment: A main entity relation between a creative work and the primary entity it describes. Also called: primary subject, about entity, central topic. Examples: "Wikipedia Article mainEntity Albert Einstein", "News Report mainEntity The Election", "Research Paper mainEntity Quantum Physics". Distinct from mainEntityOfPage, which indicates the page for which this thing is the main entity.

candidates.label: includedComposition
candidates.comment: A composition inclusion relation between a music composition and a smaller music composition that is part of it. Also called part of composition, contains composition, movement of. Examples: "A symphony has an included composition as a movement.", "A musical work includes a composition.", "This composition contains several included compositions.". Distinct from hasPart, which is a general part-whole relation for creative works.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: members
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: includes members, comprises, consists of. Examples: "Club Organization members John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership members Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization members Partner Company". Distinct from member, which is a singular form and essentially the same concept.

candidates.label: hasPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a creative work and another creative work that is a component of it. Also called includes part, contains component, component of. Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Distinct from includedComposition, which is specific to music compositions.

candidates.label: hasDefinedTerm
candidates.comment: A term inclusion relation between a defined term set or taxon and one of its contained defined terms. Also called contains term, includes term, term within. Examples: "A medical glossary has a defined term for 'hypertension'.", "A taxonomy has a defined term for 'Homo sapiens'.", "The dictionary has a defined term for 'algorithm'."

candidates.label: includesAttraction
candidates.comment: An attraction inclusion relation between a tourist destination and a tourist attraction located within it. Also called contains attraction, destination attraction, features attraction. Examples: "A tourist destination includes an attraction like a museum.", "The city includes an attraction for historical sites.", "This destination features a famous includes attraction."

candidates.label: observationAbout
candidates.comment: An entity, often a place, that an observation is about or associated with. Also called observed entity, subject of observation, related to observation. Examples: "Weather Observation observationAbout 'London'", "Patient Vitals Observation observationAbout 'John Doe'", "Traffic Count Observation observationAbout 'Main Street'".

candidates.label: manufacturer
candidates.comment: A manufacturing relation between a product and the organization that produced it. Also called: produced by, made by, fabricated by. Examples: "Smartphone manufacturer Apple", "Automobile manufacturer Toyota", "Furniture manufacturer IKEA".

candidates.label: founder
candidates.comment: A founder relation between an organization and the person or organization that established it. Also called: established by, created by, initiated by. Examples: "Microsoft" founder "Bill Gates", "Apple Inc." founder "Steve Jobs", "Google" founder "Larry Page". Distinct from founders, which is specifically for multiple people.

candidates.label: creator
candidates.comment: An authorship relation between a creative work or user comment and the person or organization responsible for its creation. Also called: author, originator, producer, made by. Examples: "Novel" creator "Jane Doe", "Software" creator "Acme Corp.", "Blog Post" creator "John Smith", "User Review" creator "Anonymous User". Distinct from copyrightHolder, which is about legal ownership.

candidates.label: editor
candidates.comment: An editor relation between a creative work and the person who edited it. Also called "edited by", "compiled by", "prepared by". Examples: "Book 'The Great Gatsby' editor 'Maxwell Perkins'", "Journal article editor 'Dr. Jane Doe'", "Film 'Pulp Fiction' editor 'Sally Menke'".

candidates.label: publisher
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a creative work or financial incentive and the organization or person that publishes it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book has a publisher 'Penguin Random House'.", "A research paper has a publisher 'Nature Publishing Group'.", "A financial incentive has a publisher 'Government Agency'.". Distinct from publishedBy, which refers to the agent of a specific publication event.

candidates.label: publishedBy
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a publication event and the organization or person responsible for it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book's publication event was published by 'Penguin Random House'.", "A journal article's publication event was published by 'Elsevier'.", "A blog post's publication event was published by 'Jane Doe'.". Distinct from publisher, which refers to the publisher of the creative work itself.

candidates.label: recognizedBy
candidates.comment: A recognition relation between a credential and the organization that acknowledges its validity or value. Also called accredited by, validated by, acknowledged by. Examples: "A university degree is recognized by 'the Ministry of Education'.", "A professional certification is recognized by 'an industry association'.", "A medical license is recognized by 'the Medical Board'."

candidates.label: creativeWorkStatus
candidates.comment: A lifecycle stage relation between a creative work and its current status. Also called: work status, publication status, development stage. Examples: "Draft Novel" creative work status "Draft", "Published Article" creative work status "Published", "Archived Website" creative work status "Obsolete", "In-progress Film" creative work status "Incomplete".

candidates.label: byMonthDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the month on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "day of month", "monthly day recurrence", "on day of month". Examples: "Rent payment schedule byMonthDay 1", "Board meeting schedule byMonthDay 15".

candidates.label: founders
candidates.comment: A founders relation between an organization and the people who established it. Also called: co-founders, creators, originators. Examples: "Google" founders "Larry Page, Sergey Brin", "Apple Inc." founders "Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak, Ronald Wayne", "Microsoft" founders "Bill Gates, Paul Allen". Distinct from founder, which can be a single person or organization.

candidates.label: accountablePerson
candidates.comment: An accountable person relation between a creative work and the individual legally responsible for it. Also called legally responsible person, liable party, responsible individual. Examples: "A news article's accountable person is its editor-in-chief.", "A company report's accountable person is the CEO."

candidates.label: diversityStaffingReport
candidates.comment: A diversity staffing report relation between an organization (e.g., news media) and an article or URL containing a report on staffing diversity issues. Also called "staff diversity report", "workforce diversity data", "inclusion metrics report". Examples: "News media organization diversityStaffingReport 'Article on newsroom diversity'", "Company diversityStaffingReport 'URL to annual diversity report'", "Organization diversityStaffingReport 'Self-reported staffing data'".

candidates.label: reportNumber
candidates.comment: A report number relation between a report and the unique identifier assigned by its publisher. Also called report ID, document number. Examples: "A financial report has a report number 'FY2023-Q4'.", "A technical report has a report number 'TR-001-2024'.", "A government report has a report number 'GAO-24-123'."

candidates.label: sourceOrganization
candidates.comment: An affiliation relation between a creative work and the organization on whose behalf its creator was working. Also called "commissioning organization", "producing organization", "organization behind", "publisher organization". Examples: "The research paper's sourceOrganization was MIT", "The documentary's sourceOrganization was BBC", "This report's sourceOrganization is the World Health Organization."

candidates.label: reviewedBy
candidates.comment: The person or organization responsible for reviewing the content of a webpage for accuracy or completeness. Also called content reviewer, page editor, accuracy checker. Examples: `Medical Information Page` reviewedBy `Dr. Jane Doe`, `News Article` reviewedBy `Fact-Checking Organization`, `Research Paper` reviewedBy `Peer Review Board`. Distinct from `author`, which indicates who created the content, not who reviewed it.

candidates.label: employmentUnit
candidates.comment: An employment unit relation between a job posting and the organization (department, unit, or facility) where the job is performed. Also called "department", "work unit", "reporting unit". Examples: "Job posting 'Software Engineer' employmentUnit 'Engineering Department'", "Job 'Sales Associate' employmentUnit 'Retail Store #123'", "Job 'HR Specialist' employmentUnit 'Human Resources Division'".

candidates.label: author
candidates.comment: An organization or person who created content or a rating. Also called: creator, writer, originator, composer. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Novel' author 'Jane Austen'", "Rating 'Product Review' author 'Consumer Reports'", "CreativeWork 'Article' author 'New York Times'". Distinct from artist, which is typically for visual or comic art.

candidates.label: publishingPrinciples
candidates.comment: A publishing principles relation between a creative work, organization, or person and the document outlining their editorial and ethical guidelines as a publisher. Also called editorial guidelines, ethics policy, publishing policy. Examples: "A news organization has publishing principles outlined on its website.", "A research journal adheres to specific publishing principles.", "A blogger follows certain publishing principles for their content."

candidates.label: recognizedBy
candidates.comment: A recognition relation between a credential and the organization that acknowledges its validity or value. Also called accredited by, validated by, acknowledged by. Examples: "A university degree is recognized by 'the Ministry of Education'.", "A professional certification is recognized by 'an industry association'.", "A medical license is recognized by 'the Medical Board'."

candidates.label: parentOrganization
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between an organization and the larger organization it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is a division of, is a subsidiary of, is part of. Examples: Google is a parent organization of YouTube. A local branch is a parent organization of its national headquarters. A department is a parent organization of its university. Distinct from subOrganization, which points from a larger organization to its smaller components.

candidates.label: acquiredFrom
candidates.comment: An acquired from relation between ownership information and the organization or person from whom a product was obtained. Also called purchased from, obtained from, source of acquisition. Examples: "The car's ownership info indicates it was acquired from 'Dealership X'.", "The book's ownership info shows it was acquired from 'John Doe'."

candidates.label: buyer
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sell action, indicating the organization or person who purchased the object. Also called "purchaser", "customer", "acquired by". Examples: "Online purchase sell action buyer Jane Doe", "Company acquisition sell action buyer Acme Corp". Distinct from seller, which is the party offering the object for sale.

candidates.label: purchaseDate
candidates.comment: A purchase date relation between a product or vehicle and the date it was acquired by its current owner. Also called acquired on, bought on, ownership date. Examples: "A car has a purchase date of 2020-05-10.", "A smartphone has a purchase date of 2023-01-15.", "A house has a purchase date of 2018-07-22.". Distinct from productionDate, which is the date the item was manufactured.

candidates.label: ownedFrom
candidates.comment: The date and time when ownership of a product was obtained. Also called acquisition date, purchase date, date acquired. Examples: "Car OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2020-01-15'", "House OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2018-06-01T10:00:00'", "Book OwnershipInfo ownedFrom '2023-03-10'". Distinct from ownedThrough, which is the date ownership ended.

candidates.label: acquireLicensePage
candidates.comment: An acquire license page relation between a creative work and the web page or resource detailing how its licenses can be obtained. Also called licensing information page, purchase license URL, rights acquisition page. Examples: "A stock photo's acquire license page is its licensing terms URL.", "A software's acquire license page describes its purchase options."

candidates.label: acceptedOffer
candidates.comment: An accepted offer relation between an order and the specific offer(s) that were agreed upon and included in it. Also called purchased offer, confirmed offer, included offer. Examples: "A customer's order accepted an offer for a laptop.", "The order accepted an offer for two books."

candidates.label: isGift
candidates.comment: A transaction intent relation indicating whether an order was placed as a gift for a recipient other than the buyer. Also called gift purchase, purchased as gift, gift order. Examples: An order has isGift set to 'true'. A purchase has isGift set to 'false'. A book order has isGift set to 'true' with gift wrapping.

candidates.label: owns
candidates.comment: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.

candidates.label: owner
candidates.comment: A person or organization that owns a thing. Also called proprietor, possessor, title holder. Examples: "Car owner 'John Doe'", "Company owner 'Acme Corp'", "House owner 'Smith Family Trust'". Distinct from creator, who made the thing.

candidates.label: orderedItem
candidates.comment: An item (product, service, or another order item) that has been ordered. Also called purchased item, item in order, ordered product. Examples: "Order 123 orderedItem 'Laptop X'", "OrderItem A orderedItem 'Software License'", "Subscription Order orderedItem 'Premium Service'".

candidates.label: productionCompany
candidates.comment: A production relation between a creative work (like a movie or series) and the organization responsible for its creation. Also called produced by, studio, made by, created by. Examples: "The movie 'Dune' was produced by Legendary Pictures.", "The TV series 'The Crown' was produced by Left Bank Pictures.", "The video game 'Cyberpunk 2077' was produced by CD Projekt Red."

candidates.label: manufacturer
candidates.comment: A manufacturing relation between a product and the organization that produced it. Also called: produced by, made by, fabricated by. Examples: "Smartphone manufacturer Apple", "Automobile manufacturer Toyota", "Furniture manufacturer IKEA".

candidates.label: countryOfOrigin
candidates.comment: A provenance relation between a creative work or product and its country of origin. Also called: origin country, produced in, made in. Examples: "French Wine" country of origin "France", "Japanese Anime" country of origin "Japan", "German Car" country of origin "Germany", "Hollywood Movie" country of origin "United States". Distinct from countryOfAssembly, which specifies where the product was put together.

candidates.label: creator
candidates.comment: An authorship relation between a creative work or user comment and the person or organization responsible for its creation. Also called: author, originator, producer, made by. Examples: "Novel" creator "Jane Doe", "Software" creator "Acme Corp.", "Blog Post" creator "John Smith", "User Review" creator "Anonymous User". Distinct from copyrightHolder, which is about legal ownership.

candidates.label: produces
candidates.comment: An outcome relation between a service and the tangible thing it generates or provides. Also called generates, yields, creates, provides. Examples: A government service produces a 'passport'. A licensing service produces a 'permit'. A printing service produces 'documents'.

candidates.label: material
candidates.comment: A material composition relation between a creative work or product and the material it is made from. Also called: made of, composed of, constructed from. Examples: "Wooden Chair material Wood", "Wool Sweater material Wool", "Paper Book material Paper".

candidates.label: producer
candidates.comment: A creative role relation between a creative work and the person or organization responsible for its production. Also called production company, executive producer, creator, maker. Examples: A movie has a producer 'Steven Spielberg'. A music album has a producer 'Universal Music Group'. A TV series has a producer 'Shonda Rhimes'. Distinct from director, who is responsible for the creative vision.

candidates.label: result
candidates.comment: The outcome or product generated by an action. Also called outcome, product, output, consequence. Examples: `WriteAction` result `Book`, `CookAction` result `Meal`, `CreateAction` result `Artwork`. Distinct from `resultComment` and `resultReview` which are specific types of results.

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: productionDate
candidates.comment: A production date relation between a product or vehicle and the specific date it was manufactured. Also called manufactured on, made on, creation date. Examples: "A 2023 Toyota Camry has a production date of 2022-11-15.", "A vintage car has a production date of 1965-03-01.", "A smartphone has a production date of 2024-01-20."

candidates.label: study
candidates.comment: A relation between a medical entity and a medical study or trial that investigates it. Also called "related study", "investigated by study", "medical trial". Examples: "The drug has study a clinical trial", "The medical condition is part of a study", "This therapy is being evaluated in a study."

candidates.label: studySubject
candidates.comment: An investigative relation between a medical study and the medical entity (condition, therapy, drug, etc.) that is being investigated. Also called "subject of investigation", "research focus", "entity studied", "trial subject". Examples: "The medical study has studySubject a new drug", "The clinical trial's studySubject is a specific medical condition", "This study investigates a studySubject therapy."

candidates.label: assesses
candidates.comment: A relation between a creative work, education event, or learning resource and the competency or learning outcome it is intended to evaluate. Also called: evaluates, measures, tests, gauges. Examples: "LearningResource 'Quiz' assesses 'Understanding of Algebra'", "EducationEvent 'Exam' assesses 'Problem-solving skills'", "CreativeWork 'Rubric' assesses 'Writing proficiency'."

candidates.label: measurementTechnique
candidates.comment: A measurement technique relation between a data catalog, data download, dataset, observation, property value, or statistical variable and the technique, method, or technology used for measurement. Also called: measurement approach, data collection method, analytical technique. Examples: "Molecule Concentration Dataset measurementTechnique 'Mass Spectrometry'", "Depression Rating Observation measurementTechnique 'Beck Depression Inventory'", "Water Quality Data measurementTechnique 'Chromatography'". Distinct from measurementMethod, which is a more specific subproperty.

candidates.label: studyDesign
candidates.comment: A specification of the design methodology for a medical observational study. Also called "observational study type", "research design", "study methodology". Examples: "The study has studyDesign CohortStudy", "The medical observational study's studyDesign is CrossSectionalStudy", "This research uses a studyDesign of CaseControlStudy."

candidates.label: observationAbout
candidates.comment: An entity, often a place, that an observation is about or associated with. Also called observed entity, subject of observation, related to observation. Examples: "Weather Observation observationAbout 'London'", "Patient Vitals Observation observationAbout 'John Doe'", "Traffic Count Observation observationAbout 'Main Street'".

candidates.label: studyLocation
candidates.comment: A geographic relation between a medical study and the administrative area where it is conducted or was conducted. Also called "research location", "trial site", "study area", "geographic scope of study". Examples: "The medical study has studyLocation New York", "The clinical trial's studyLocation is Europe", "This study is taking place in a specific studyLocation."

candidates.label: usedToDiagnose
candidates.comment: A used to diagnose relation between a medical test and a medical condition it is employed to identify. Also called diagnoses, identifies condition, screens for. Examples: "MedicalTest 'MRI' usedToDiagnose 'Brain Tumor'", "MedicalTest 'Blood Test' usedToDiagnose 'Anemia'", "MedicalTest 'X-ray' usedToDiagnose 'Fracture'".

candidates.label: review
candidates.comment: A critical assessment or evaluation of an item, such as a product, service, or creative work. Also called item review, evaluation, critique, assessment. Examples: `Product: Smartphone` review `Customer Review`, `Movie: Inception` review `Film Critic's Review`, `Restaurant: The Fancy Bistro` review `Food Blogger's Review`. Distinct from `reviews`, which is a plural form and often implies a collection.

candidates.label: observationPeriod
candidates.comment: The length of time over which an observation took place. Also called observation duration, period of observation, measurement period. Examples: "Clinical Trial Observation observationPeriod 'P6M'", "Weather Monitoring observationPeriod 'P24h'", "Patient Tracking observationPeriod 'P1Y'". Distinct from observationDate, which is the specific point in time of the observation.

candidates.label: successorOf
candidates.comment: A lineage relation between a newer product model and its previous, often discontinued, predecessor. Also called "replaces", "evolved from", "preceded by", "derived from". Examples: "iPhone 15 is successorOf iPhone 14", "The new car model is successorOf the previous generation", "This product is a successorOf an older variant."

candidates.label: previousItem
candidates.comment: A sequential relation between a list item and the list item that immediately precedes it. Also called precedes, comes after, follows. Examples: List item 'B' has a previous item 'A'. The current item's previous item is the one before it. In a breadcrumb trail, the current page has a previous item. Distinct from nextItem, which links to the item that follows.

candidates.label: supersededBy
candidates.comment: A deprecation relation between an older term (property, class, or enumeration) and a newer term that replaces or supersedes it. Also called "replaced by", "obsoleted by", "succeeded by", "deprecated by". Examples: "OldProperty is supersededBy NewProperty", "The deprecated class is supersededBy a modern equivalent", "This enumeration value is supersededBy a more precise one."

candidates.label: beforeMedia
candidates.comment: A media object representing the circumstances prior to performing a how-to direction. Also called: pre-action media, initial state media. Examples: "HowToDirection 'Install Shelf' beforeMedia 'Image of empty wall'", "HowToDirection 'Bake Cake' beforeMedia 'Video of ingredients on counter'."

candidates.label: nextItem
candidates.comment: A list item that immediately follows the current list item in an ordered sequence. Also called subsequent item, following item, next in list. Examples: "Item 1 nextItem 'Item 2'", "Page 3 nextItem 'Page 4'", "Step A nextItem 'Step B'". Distinct from previousItem, which links to the preceding item.

candidates.label: predecessorOf
candidates.comment: A lineage relation between a product model and its newer, often superseding, variant. Also called replaced by, succeeded by, updated to, newer version is. Examples: iPhone 10 is a predecessor of iPhone 11. Model A is a predecessor of Model B. The old software version is a predecessor of the new one. Distinct from successorOf, which points from a newer variant to an older one.

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: honorificPrefix
candidates.comment: An honorific prefix relation between a person and a title preceding their name. Also called title, salutation, courtesy title. Examples: "A person has an honorific prefix 'Dr.'.", "Her honorific prefix is 'Ms.'.", "The individual uses the honorific prefix 'Mr.'."

candidates.label: tocContinuation
candidates.comment: A table of contents continuation relation between a HyperToc entry and the next default HyperToc entry to play or render. Also called next entry, subsequent entry, continued by. Examples: "Chapter 1 tocContinuation 'Chapter 2'", "Segment A tocContinuation 'Segment B'", "HyperTocEntry 'Intro' tocContinuation 'Main Content'".

candidates.label: publishedBy
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a publication event and the organization or person responsible for it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book's publication event was published by 'Penguin Random House'.", "A journal article's publication event was published by 'Elsevier'.", "A blog post's publication event was published by 'Jane Doe'.". Distinct from publisher, which refers to the publisher of the creative work itself.
